newsitem.title: USA: Coastal gets U.S. Treasury okay for Iraq oil.
newsitem.headline: Coastal gets U.S. Treasury okay for Iraq oil.

text.p: Coastal Corp has been given clearance by the U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) for its deal to lift Iraqi crude oil under the "oil-for-food" scheme with the United Nations, a U.S. government source said Thursday.
"We have approved (Coastal's) licence and transmitted it to the United Nations," the source said.

The details of Coastal's deal have not been discolsed by the company, though market sources said it is expected to be for 60,000 barrels a day (bpd). Coastal was a big buyer of Iraqi oil prior to the embargo in the wake of the invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
Coastal officials said in August that they expected to bring any Iraqi oil bought under the U.N. deal to its Aruba refinery in the Caribbean.

There are no other U.S. licenses pending, the U.S. official said, though Texaco Inc said on Wednesday that it is negotiating a deal with Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) to contract for 35,000-40,000 barrels a day.

OFAC is screening contracts that U.S. oil companies conclude with Iraq in order to ensure they comply with U.S. and U.N. regulations. Approved contracts are then passed to U.N. overseers for approval under the terms of the Iraq-U.N. deal.

On Thursday, the U.N. said it currently has four contracts under active consideration for approval. The only contract approved by the U.N. so far is Turkish state oil concern TUPRAS's 75,000 bpd deal.
Under the deal, Iraq is allowed to sell up to $2 billion of oil over six months (renewable), which at current prices is estimated to be about 550,000-600,000 bpd.
